title: AI Voice & TTS News Briefing
summary: Covers Fri Nov 13, 3:37 PM to Mon Nov 16, 7:52 AM MT. A quiet weekend: no major launches. Two Nov 13 developments not previously reported: KittenML's free Apache-2.0 KittenTTS 2 Mini/Nano/Pico on-device models (up to 16 languages incl. Hindi and Swahili) and ElevenLabs' Forward Deployed Creatives managed localization service with linguist review. Reminder: Google's Gemini TTS/Live preview models shut down Nov 17 with no redirect.

articles.title: KittenML releases KittenTTS 2 Mini, Nano and Pico: free on-device TTS in up to 16 languages
articles.summary: Three small Apache-2.0 TTS models that run on a CPU: Mini (82M parameters, ~83 MB, 16 languages incl. Hindi, Swahili, Japanese, Korean, Turkish; 118 voices), Nano and Pico (8 languages, 8-17 MB). No voice cloning and no published quality scores yet. Why it matters: a commercially usable, offline option for multilingual narration prototypes and devices without cloud costs or data leaving the network; quality in each language must be tested before production use.

articles.title: ElevenLabs launches Forward Deployed Creatives, a managed service for enterprise localization and creative production
articles.summary: ElevenLabs now pairs creative staff with enterprise teams to move AI creative work from pilots into production, or delivers finished campaigns, with linguists and audio specialists reviewing localized material and support for dubbing, voiceover, subtitles, audio description and custom voices. Why it matters: AI voice vendors are now selling managed localization with human review, competing with traditional language service providers; a benchmark for pricing and quality-control expectations. Summary source; original ElevenLabs post could not be retrieved.
